name: ABA and autism therapy

pf.license.need: the practice's own word, optional: each behavior analyst's national certification and any state license the practice names; each behavior technician's own registration; the practice's own license if it has one. Rosie never looks a license up and never says one is checked
pf.license.who: both: the practice and each analyst and technician
pf.license.ask: each analyst's certification and state license numbers; each technician's registration number and their supervising analyst; the practice's license where one exists
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks a license or background check up and never says one is checked. A background check shows only as the owner's word, with its date if the owner gives one
pf.license.scope: technicians give therapy only under a named supervising analyst, at the supervision share the certification board and the health plan require; assessments, treatment plans, plan changes and parent training are done by an analyst; any restraint only as the child's written plan and the state's rules allow, by trained staff; no diagnosis is given by the practice unless a licensed provider on its team may give one
pf.license.blocks: Rosie acts on the practice's own word only: a visit the owner says needs a credential the technician lacks isn't booked; a person the owner says is no longer approved is paused
pf.license.renewals: the owner's own reminders for expiry dates; a lapse the owner reports pauses that person's new sessions at once
pf.license.insurance: professional liability insurance where the state's form or the health plan asks for it
pf.license.background: a background check for everyone who works with children is the practice's own word, as the owner gives it; never looked up by Rosie
pf.license.telehealth: parent training by video only with an analyst licensed where the family is (where the state licenses analysts)

pf.services.shape: clinic: a child with autism gets many sessions a week (often 10 to 40 hours) on a set weekly schedule, at the center, at home, or at school or daycare with the school's OK; each session is one-to-one with a behavior technician from the child's small team, under a supervising analyst; the analyst joins some sessions to supervise and meets the parents for training; the health plan's approval sets the hours for about 6 months at a time
pf.services.examples: the example practice's own prices and lengths, not a standard

list.where: at the center or at home
list.note: by an analyst; needs the diagnosis report and the plan's approval first

list.name: Therapy session (one-to-one)
list.price: billed to the plan; $60 an hour self-pay (example)
list.where: at the center, at home, or at school or daycare

list.repeat: a set weekly schedule (example Monday to Friday, 9am to noon) for the length of the plan's approval
list.note: with a technician from the child's team

list.note: the analyst joins the technician; both must be free

list.name: Social skills group
list.note: 4 to 6 children of about the same age; one staff for every 3 children; at least 3 children to run (the practice's cutoff, 2 days before)

list.name: Reassessment
list.where: at the center or at home
list.note: every 6 months, before the plan's approval ends

pf.services.capacity: each child has a small team (example 2 or 3 technicians trained on that child's plan) and one supervising analyst; a technician has one child at a time; a center session uses a therapy room; a supervised session needs the analyst and the technician at the same time
pf.services.schedule: a weekly schedule is set at the start for the length of the plan's approval; each session is one visit of a repeat plan
pf.services.online: parent training by video; it counts as at the center
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: a parent or caregiver adult stays home during home sessions (the practice's rule)

where therapy would happen: at the center, at home, or at school or daycare
how many hours a week the family hopes for, and which days and times work

securePage: the diagnosis report and the doctor's referral the plan needs

pf.questions.whoMayBook: a parent or legal guardian books for the child and consents; where parents are separated, the papers on the secure page decide who may book, consent and pick up; a school or daycare never books, but gives its written OK for sessions there; an adult with autism books for themselves or with their guardian

stop.words: a child is missing (ran off from the center or a home session), a seizure over 5 minutes, trouble breathing, or a serious injury
stop.say: This sounds like an emergency. If anyone is in danger, get to safety and call 911 now.
stop.booking: no booking; the parent is called at once

stop.words: suicide or self-harm words from a parent, a teen, or the child
stop.say: If you're thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 now. If you're in danger right now, call 911.
stop.booking: 988 and 911 first, at once, any hour; no booking in that chat until a clear 'I'm safe right now'; the analyst is told the same day

goOn.words: self-injury or aggression that's getting worse
goOn.what: the analyst is told privately the same day; a safety review before the next session

goOn.words: a report of abuse or neglect of a child
goOn.what: the practice's staff report as the law requires; Rosie gives the state's child abuse hotline from its safety list and tells a person on Rosie's team the same day; never asks for details by text

goOn.words: asks about medicines or a diagnosis
goOn.what: never answered by Rosie: the analyst or the child's doctor

pf.safety.always: the generic screen: danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency → 911, and no booking; a child's details are never asked by text

pf.first_steps.prep: for the reminder: the child's snack and water, a change of clothes, any toys or rewards the analyst asked for, and any communication device; for home sessions, a quiet space and an adult at home

pf.visit.checkIn: at the center: the parent gives the check-in code at the desk and signs the child in; pick-up only by an adult on the approved list, with photo ID; at home: the code at the door and a parent or caregiver stays home; at school: the school's own sign-in, then the code
pf.visit.changes: the analyst updates the treatment plan and the hours: a change in hours is a new schedule the parent OKs, and the plan's approval may be needed first; nothing is sold at a session
pf.visit.cantGoAhead: the child is sick (fever or vomiting, the practice's sick rule), no adult is home for a home session, the plan's approval has ended, or the technician can't come and nobody on the child's team can: the session is cancelled with no fee
pf.visit.done: the code at drop-off, then DONE from the technician once the session note is done in the practice's own records; session data and progress reports stay in the practice's records; the parent gets a short daily note on the secure page; Rosie keeps only booking records
pf.visit.incidents: an injury, a restraint, or a child running off during a session: the parent is called at once and gets a written incident report the same day

pf.money.before: most families take nothing when booking (the plan pays); self-pay families save a card, charged once a week for that week's sessions
pf.money.insurance: health plans: only the plan's name before times; member details on the secure page; the practice asks for the plan's approval for the hours and bills the plan; copays or the family's share are billed once a month in one bill; public program families pay nothing
pf.money.approval: the plan approves a number of hours a week until an end date (about 6 months); sessions are booked only inside the approved hours and dates; the practice asks for a renewal, with a reassessment, before it ends
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form
pf.money.fees: no missed-session fee by default; a late-cancel fee only if the owner sets one at sign-up and confirms it for each case; never billed to a plan or a public program
pf.money.payOverTime: the practice's own payment plan, only if the owner turns it on
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to every kind of work, health included: a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee

pf.messages.never: the child's diagnosis, behaviors, health, session data, progress and plan details never go in a text: only the secure page; texts say only the practice's name, the day, the time and the place, and name the child only by first initial
pf.messages.staffTexts: technicians and the owner get the child's initials, the time and the place; behavior and health notes stay on the secure page
pf.messages.minors: every text goes to the parent or guardian; separated parents each get texts only as the custody papers allow
pf.messages.school: Rosie never texts the school; the parent forwards the school its OK link
pf.messages.displayName: a switch: the practice texts under a plain display name, Lee Family Care or Lee Home Care; card statements show it too

pf.staff.licenses: analysts certified (and licensed where the state requires); technicians registered and supervised
pf.staff.skills: behavior analyst, behavior technician, trained on a given child's plan (per child), parent training, social skills groups, home sessions, school sessions, toddlers, Spanish, sign language
pf.staff.supervision: each technician has a named supervising analyst who supervises at the share the board and the plan require (the analyst joins sessions)
pf.staff.oks: the analyst OKs plan changes, a new technician on a child's team, and a return after an incident; the owner OKs schedule changes and fees
pf.staff.standIn: only a technician already trained on this child's plan (on the child's team), and the parent is told before the session; nobody new is sent to a child without the parent's yes; nobody on the team free: the session is cancelled with no fee
pf.staff.ratio: one technician per child in therapy sessions; one staff for every 3 children in groups
pf.staff.away: home and school sessions only by staff cleared for them

pf.rules.privacy: a health privacy agreement (a business associate agreement) is signed before going live; children's details only on the secure page
pf.rules.records: a child's records are kept as long as the state's rules require (often until some years after the child turns 18); never deleted on request while the rules say keep them; Rosie keeps only booking records
pf.rules.consent: a parent's or guardian's written consent for treatment, for any restraint in the plan, and for photos or video; separate releases for the school or other providers
pf.rules.restraint: only as the child's written plan and the state's rules allow; every use written down and the parent told the same day
pf.rules.reporting: staff are required to report suspected child abuse or neglect to the state's hotline
pf.rules.school: sessions at school only with the school's written OK and the parent's consent
pf.rules.showFacts: the analyst's certification and license shown where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.reviews: a rating may be asked of a parent at most once a quarter, never after an incident; any reply never confirms the family is a client

pf.edges.approvalEnds: the plan's approval is about to end: the reassessment is booked before; not renewed: sessions stop or turn self-pay only with the parent's yes
pf.edges.techSick: a technician can't come: only a technician on the child's team, with the parent told before; nobody: cancelled with no fee
pf.edges.childSick: the child is sick: cancelled with no fee under the practice's sick rule
pf.edges.latePickup: a parent is late to pick up: the child stays with staff; the parent, then the emergency contact, is called
pf.edges.notDroppedOff: a child not dropped off for a center session: the parent is called, no fee words
pf.edges.runsOff: a child runs off: 911 and the parent at once
pf.edges.incident: an injury or restraint: the parent is called at once and gets a written report the same day
pf.edges.custody: separated parents: the papers decide who books, consents, gets texts and picks up
pf.edges.school: school sessions: the school's written OK first
pf.edges.manySessions: many sessions a week: one repeat plan; reminders and ratings must not flood the family
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way

notes:
Refit Tue Oct 27 2026 (R12) to the REDESIGN 2 master: facts planbill, forms, plans, video, children, firststeps, results; sensitive on; welfare on in flow B only; no $2 (S1-62 off); setstart both flows; cutoff 24 hours before (A) and 7am the day of (B). Money A list|none|counter (main; Speech and language evaluation $140, the $35 copay in the example), list|card|counter (fee $20), list|card|card (Speech therapy session $110, fee $20). Money B list|none|own (main; Home evaluation $179) and list|card|card (fee $89). Every old words op is gone; own steps kept (referral check, plan of care and weekly series, progress check, hearing screen), with their money variants folded into one line true on every path. The home company is now Lee Home Speech (word limits).
From: physical-therapist (built from the dentist clinic pilot, reviewed). Why: a speech practice runs like it: an evaluation by a licensed therapist, then a plan of care with a weekly series booked by the client's own yes, plans checked by hand, video sessions only where the therapist is licensed for where the client is, home visits on the other side, and no $2 for a health practice. What it lacked came from the pediatrician overlay: a parent or guardian books for a child, who may bring the child is a switch, and children's details stay on the secure page.
Names: Sam Lee, a speech therapist, owns Lee Home Speech (the master's main company: home speech therapy and hearing care, 520 Main St, a 25-mile area) and Lee Speech Therapy (the second company: the clinic, 30 Cedar Ave). Flow A's story is at the clinic: Alex's daughter Lily, 4. Flow B's is at the family's home, 9 Aspen Ln: Alex's son Max, 2.
People: at the clinic, Iris (speech therapist; Spanish; feeding work; the clinic's home visits) and Elise (speech therapist, Saturday afternoons). On the home team, Caleb (speech therapist, also a licensed audiologist, feeding work) and Tia (speech therapy assistant, sessions only, under a therapist's plan). Sam, Pat and Alex M. stay. The pilot's people are all renamed; other clients keep master names (Dee W., Ben T., Nia K., Lin W., Morgan P., Kim L.) or new ones (Nora S., Ruth P., Ivy C.).
Kinds of work: plumbing became home speech therapy, electrical became hearing care (it waits for its audiologist's license), the barbershop became the clinic. Licenses are switches from the state's form: each speech therapist's own license (Sam's SP045210), an assistant's or a clinical fellow's credential where the state asks, an audiologist's license for hearing care, and the practice's registration (PR20981) only where asked.
Who books: a parent or legal guardian for anyone under 18 (Rosie's rule for this work until a state's form says otherwise; the minor-consent age is a switch); an adult for themselves; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent, like after a stroke (Rosa for her mother). Anyone else is asked to have a parent book. Who may bring the child is a switch: a parent, or an adult the parent OKs on the secure page (A8-02, A8-51 to A8-60, B4-26, B4-27). At a preschool session, the parent signs an OK and stays reachable by phone (S1-59, B4-66).
Privacy: the AI hears only the kind of visit, the child's age, the languages at home, a school plan yes or no, a referral yes or not yet, and the plan's name. The child's name, birth date, the reason, test results and health history go only on the secure page. Customer texts carry the business, date, time and place, never the child's name or the visit type; an extra service in a text is 'one more thing' or 'the extra visit', with what it is on the secure page. Owner and staff texts use initials (L.M., M.M. for the child; A.M. for the parent) and a link. At home the therapist's name stays, for the door check.
Safety: stroke signs at any age (sudden trouble speaking, a drooping face, weakness on one side), choking now or trouble breathing get 'Call 911 now' and no booking; self-harm words get 988 and 911. Coughing at meals with no choking now gets the 911 words first, then the booking goes on (A3-23, B3-18, B7-17). Rosie never judges how serious anything is.
Prices are the example practices' own, not a standard: clinic evaluation $140 (75 min), session $110 (45 min), re-check $120, adult evaluation $140, voice check $40 (the one recording room), feeding evaluation $160 with Sam's OK, hearing screening $20 added to an evaluation, video session $110, a plan's $35 copay, a $20 late-cancel or missed-visit fee only where Sam turns it on. Home: evaluation $179 (75 min), session $150, mealtime visit $160, adult evaluation at home $199 ($249 with Sam), an $89 fee for self-pay visits only. Hearing care: $60 hearing test, $20 ear check, preschool screenings $120 an hour.
Money A: list|none|counter is the main path: nothing taken; the desk checks the plan by hand; the copay at the front desk at each visit; self-pay families pay the list price there, and a family whose plan the clinic doesn't take gets a receipt to send its plan (A9-03, A9-20, A8-x04). list|card|counter: the clinic's $20 late-cancel fee, free to cancel until 24 hours before, a card saved for it, Sam confirms each charge, never for a fee-free family. list|card|card: Saturday mornings with no front desk, and video sessions: the card is charged at DONE. Left out: holds, deposits and full price (therapy is never paid ahead), photos and visit pricing (every service is on the list), Rosie's texted bill (the clinic has a front desk).
Money B: list|none|own is the main path (the office bills the family's plan its own way). list|card|card is self-pay: a card saved, $179 charged at DONE, and an $89 fee after 7am on the day only if Sam confirms it. A self-pay family hears about the written price estimate before saying yes (B4-28). Left out: holds, deposits, full price, a texted bill, photos and visit pricing.
Sign-up words follow that (S1-12 to S1-18, S1-41 to S1-47): plan families book with nothing taken; self-pay home families save a card; the clinic saves a card only for its fee or a Saturday-morning visit. No tips, no bank transfer, no $2 (S1-26, S1-62, S1-65).
Referral: a switch from the state's form (A4-x01 to A4-x03, B4-x01 to B4-x03): not needed to evaluate (the story); allowed with limits (marked 'no referral', only therapists the state allows, the desk counts the limit); needed first (nothing booked). Where the plan wants one before weekly sessions, the office asks the child's doctor itself with the parent's OK (A4-48, B4-42), and the sessions wait for it.
Public programs: said once, as information (Rosie's rule): a child 3 or older can get a free evaluation from the school district (A4-50); under 3, the state's early intervention program (B4-05). Speech services in a school plan are never booked: the school district gives them (A4-38).
Own steps: A8-x09 and A8-x10, a pass-or-fail hearing screening when Alex adds it (refer to an audiologist if not passed; sessions can still start). After the evaluation, Iris sets the plan of care (A8-x01), the desk records the plan's OK (A8-x02: 12 sessions until Fri Jan 29; pending; or self-pay), and the weekly plan goes out for Alex's own yes (A8-x05 to A8-x08: Tuesdays 3:30pm, after preschool). Flow B does the same for 12 weekly home sessions, mostly with Tia under Caleb's plan (B8-x01 to B8-x05). A10-x01 and A10-x02: a progress check at the 6th session, and a desk warning before the plan's OK or its yearly visit limit runs out.
